trainedOn.domain: Sentinel-1 VV decibels, the scenes supplied with this project
trainedOn.labelRule: a dark region counts as oil when the supplied reference mask covers >= 50% of it and as not-oil when it covers <= 5%; the rest are dropped rather than guessed at
trainedOn.proposerNote: the proposer is the same code that runs on the look-alike set and is given no reference mask; its recall of the labelled oil is reported so a high screening score cannot hide a proposer that simply missed the slick

proposer.rule: pixels at or below mean - 1 standard deviations of the scene's own valid water, smoothed first, cleaned up morphologically, then anything under 400 px discarded

components.note: the same screen applied to what the segmentation network published. The patch counts above are darkness proposals over the whole scene, cut by a threshold rather than by the network, so the two sets of verdicts can disagree about the same water

features.name: darknessZ
features.label: darkness against local water
features.rationale: oil damps the short capillary waves the radar sees, so a film sits several standard deviations below the water around it; a low-wind patch is shallower because the water is only slightly smoother, not covered

features.name: darknessP10Z
features.label: darkness of the darkest tenth
features.rationale: a mean can be dragged down by a few very dark pixels, so the tenth percentile asks whether the whole region is dark or only part of it

features.name: textureRatio
features.label: interior roughness
features.rationale: a damped surface is smoother than the sea around it, so its pixel spread is narrower; wind shadows and blooms stay as speckled as open water

features.name: edgeSharpness
features.label: edge definition
features.rationale: a film has a physical boundary and the backscatter steps across it; a low-wind zone fades, so its edge gradient is no stronger than the ambient texture

features.name: compactness
features.label: compactness
features.rationale: spills are drawn out by wind and current into ragged forms; a compact blob is more consistent with a wind cell or a bloom patch

features.name: solidity
features.label: solidity
features.rationale: a slick feathers at its edges and leaves gaps inside its hull; a smooth convex region is a weaker candidate

features.name: elongation
features.label: elongation
features.rationale: a discharge from a moving vessel is linear, and wind stretches any film along its axis, so elongation argues for oil -- though a ship wake is linear too, which is why this feature is never decisive on its own

limits: the screen separates oil-like from not-oil-like; it cannot name the phenomenon, so a rejected patch is never called algae, low wind or a wake
a patch that falls between the two thresholds is returned as uncertain and kept: suppressing a detection the screen is unsure of would trade a measured false positive for an unmeasured missed spill

these patches are darkness proposals, not detections. A rejected patch that overlaps no published slick was never in this case to begin with -- it is evidence about what the screen would have thrown out, not a correction to the 1 slick above

forcing.label: Drift forcing: Synthetic scenario data
forcing.method: surface current is the curl of a streamfunction made of three travelling modes at the M2, K1 and M4 tidal periods over a steady background drift, so the flow is analytically non-divergent

amplitudeAnchor.source: CMEMS product, measured over this scene's footprint
amplitudeAnchor.note: the magnitude is taken from the real product even though its timestep does not match the acquisition; only the scale is borrowed, not the flow pattern

wind.note: a uniform wind vector rotating on a fixed period, drawn from the scene's own seed; plausible in magnitude and invented in direction

forcing.windNote: oil also moves at 3% of a synthetic 6.0 m/s wind, i.e. 0.181 m/s, comparable to the 0.063 m/s current - as it is in reality, where wind drift often dominates

landMask.source: CMEMS no-data cells (land is where both velocity components are NaN)

landMask.validity: coastlines do not move between the acquisition dates and the product date, so this mask is used even though the currents are not

spillAge.caveat: The interval is bounded by the drift horizon, not measured. It inherits every limitation of the forcing it was computed from.

ais.label: AIS mode: Synthetic demonstration data
ais.disclaimer: These vessel tracks are fabricated for demonstration. They are not evidence, they describe no real voyage, and no real vessel was near the imaged slick.
ais.identifierNote: MMSI numbers begin 999, which is outside the ITU Maritime Identification Digits range (201-775), so none of these identifiers can belong to a real vessel.
ais.nameNote: Names are placeholders of the form 'SYNTHETIC DEMO <word>' and are not drawn from any vessel registry.
ais.imoNote: The IMO field is deliberately empty. Every 7-digit IMO number is either allocated to a real ship or reserved by the IMO, so unlike MMSI -- where the 999 prefix is unassigned -- there is no synthetic-safe range to draw from, and a fabricated number would be some real vessel's. An empty IMO is also what 48.6% of rows in a real MarineCadastre file carry, so the gap is realistic as well as safe.
ais.callSignNote: Call signs are of the form QDEMOnnn. The ITU allocates no international call-sign series beginning with Q -- the letter is reserved for Q-codes -- so no real station can hold one of these.

schema.label: synthetic (MarineCadastre schema)

sentinels.Heading: 511.0 -> None
sentinels.IMO: blank, or IMO followed by all zeros / fewer than 7 significant digits -> None

sentinels.Status: blank -> None (always the case for TransceiverClass B)

schema.note: Field names, order, units and coded values follow NOAA's AIS data dictionary and VesselTypeCodes2018. A real daily extract can be read by spilltrace_drift.marinecadastre.read_csv with no other change.

attribution.status: Status: Research PoC - human review required
attribution.caveat: This ranking is a triage aid computed from synthetic AIS and synthetic drift forcing. It is not evidence, it does not establish responsibility, and every entry requires human verification against licensed AIS and observed metocean data.

method.distance: great-circle distance to the drift envelope centre at the vessel's own timestamp, full marks inside 1 envelope radii and zero beyond 3
method.time: half for being within reach of the estimated oil position during the release window, half scaling to 6 h of such coverage
method.trajectory: two thirds for intersecting the envelope, one third for a course across the drift axis, both gated on proximity
method.behaviour: full marks below 1 kn near the closest approach, partial for a relative drop
method.type: category relevance to bulk oil carriage
method.dataCompleteness: 60% report completeness, 40% field completeness, penalised for rejected rows

releaseWindow.basis: the span covered by the backward drift run: oil seen at the acquisition could have entered the water at any time within it

filtering.rule: A vessel is relevant only if the same AIS report satisfies both halves of the test: it falls inside the estimated release window, and it lies within 3 drift-envelope radii of where the oil is estimated to have been at that report's own timestamp. Everything else is irrelevant traffic: present in the scene, but not near the oil when the oil was there.
filtering.retentionNote: Excluded vessels are still scored and retained, ranked below the relevant ones, so that the filter itself can be audited. Filtering here means separating the traffic that can support a release from the traffic that cannot, not deleting records.
filtering.summary: 782 AIS reports · 10 vessels → 9 with reports in the release window → 2 intersect the origin envelope (within 3 envelope radii) → 8 excluded as irrelevant traffic

previews.label: Satellite imagery: Supplied Sentinel-1 SAR dataset

limits: AIS traffic is synthetic. No real vessel appears anywhere in this product.
Drift forcing may be synthetic. Real CMEMS currents are used only when the product covers the scene in both space and time, and every screen states which mode it used.
Rankings are triage aids. Nothing here establishes responsibility for a discharge.

Accuracy comes from held-out patches, not from the field. The split is grouped by parent acquisition so no acquisition appears on both sides of it, which makes this an honest test-set score and not a field-validated detection rate.
Look-alike screening separates oil-like from not-oil-like. It does not identify the phenomenon, so no rejected patch is called algae, low wind or a wake.
